item.title: Atlantic Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABNT20 KNHC 270526
TWOAT

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
200 AM EDT Sun Sep 27 2026

For the North Atlantic...Caribbean Sea and the Gulf of America:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Depression Fay, located well to the west-southwest of the Azores.

Central Subtropical Atlantic:
A surface trough of low pressure located several hundred miles to
the southeast of Bermuda is currently producing an area of
disorganized showers and thunderstorms. Environmental conditions
could become favorable for gradual development of this system as it
moves northward this weekend and then turns eastward by the early to
middle portion of next week.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...10 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...low...20 percent.

$$
Forecaster Evans/Pierce/Hagen

item.description:
Issued at 900 AM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026 
000
WTNT31 KNHC 270849

BULLETIN
Tropical Depression Fay Advisory Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026
 
...FAY HOLDING STEADY AS IT MOVES SOUTHWARD...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 900 AM GMT...0900 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...29.2N 43.9W
ABOUT 1145 MI...1840 KM WSW OF THE AZORES
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...35 MPH...55 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...S OR 175 DEGREES AT 3 MPH...6 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...1010 MB...29.83 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 900 AM GMT (0900 UTC), the center of Tropical Depression Fay was
located near latitude 29.2 North, longitude 43.9 West. The
depression is moving toward the south near 3 mph (6 km/h). A 
gradual turn to the southwest and then west is expected over the 
next couple of days, along with an increase in forward speed. 
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 35 mph (55 km/h) with higher gusts.
Little change in strength is forecast over the next several days. 
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 1010 mb (29.83 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
None.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 300 PM GMT.
 
$$
Forecaster Evans/Hagen

item.title: Tropical Depression Fay Forecast Discussion Number 29
item.description:
Issued at 900 AM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026 
475 
WTNT41 KNHC 270850
TCDAT1
 
Tropical Depression Fay Discussion Number  29
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       AL062026
900 AM GMT Sun Sep 27 2026

Fay's convection has redeveloped once again. Since the last 
advisory, an area of deep convection located just south of the 
storm's low-level center has grown in size, with cloud-top 
temperatures nearing -80°C at times. The latest subjective Dvorak 
intensity estimate from TAFB rated Fay at 1.5/25 kt, while objective 
analysis from UW-CIMSS estimates the storm's strength between 29-36 
kt. Given Fay's pulsating cycles of convection, the initial 
intensity was held steady at 30 kt, with the caveat that brief 
periods of slightly stronger max winds are entirely possible.

Initial motion remains slow at 170/3 kt. However, Fay is expected to 
gain forward speed soon as it escapes the influence of the Atlantic 
subtropical high and is picked up by the prevailing easterlies early 
next week. This will cause a turn to the southwest and then west. 
The latest track forecast is largely unchanged from the previous 
advisory, reflecting only a slight rightward shift to blend better 
with HCCA guidance.

As long as Fay remains in an environment characterized by warm SSTs, 
its cycles of pulsating convection are expected to continue. It was 
anticipated that strong vertical wind shear would work to break 
apart Fay's circulation, but the storm has proven resilient. Global 
forecast models still suggest that convection will completely 
dissipate by the middle of next week at the latest, before Fay opens 
up into a trough shortly thereafter. Little was changed in the 
latest intensity forecast. Fay is expected to waver right around 
tropical depression or even weak tropical storm strength as 
convection pulsates, before eventually dissipating for good.
 
 
FORECAST POSITIONS AND MAX WINDS
